Chiptune.subject: Indian Music & Fine Arts
Chiptune.question: The _____ was Style of synthesized electronic music.
Chiptune.fact: Chiptune, also called 8-bit music (although not all chiptune is 8-bit), is a style of electronic music and musical subculture made using the programmable sound generator (PSG) sound chips or synthesizers in vintage arcade machines, computers and video game consoles. Any existing song can be arranged in a chiptune style.

Chiptune.subject: Indian Music & Fine Arts
Chiptune.question: Common waveform generator configurations usually included two or three simple waveforms and often a single pseudo-random-noise generator (_____)
Chiptune.fact: Common waveform generator configurations usually included two or three simple waveforms and often a single pseudo-random-noise generator (PRNG).

Chiptune.subject: Indian Music & Fine Arts
Chiptune.question: Two notable examples of systems employing this technology were the _____ portable game console and the Commodore 64 personal computer
Chiptune.fact: Two notable examples of systems employing this technology were the Game Boy portable game console and the Commodore 64 personal computer. The Game Boy uses two pulse channels (switchable between 12.5%, 25%, 50% and 75% wave duty cycle), a channel for a 4-bit waveform generator, and a pseudo-random-noise generator.

Chiptune.subject: Indian Music & Fine Arts
Chiptune.question: Unlike the _____, the pulse channels on the Commodore 64 allowed full control over wave duty cycles
Chiptune.fact: Two notable examples of systems employing this technology were the Game Boy portable game console and the Commodore 64 personal computer. The Game Boy uses two pulse channels (switchable between 12.5%, 25%, 50% and 75% wave duty cycle), a channel for a 4-bit waveform generator, and a pseudo-random-noise generator.
